comparison: Both evaluate H3K4me3 binding preference claims (C7, C31, C80-C82). OpenEval finds the dCypher data supportive with minor concerns about replicates. Peer reviewers are more critical, questioning the control experiments and requesting additional peptide binding assays and charge substitution mutants to validate the acetylation mechanism interpretation.

Both evaluate TINTIN module nucleosome binding claims (C9, C33, C86-C87). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to high binding background and lack of H3K36me3 specificity. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY and request additional biochemistry beyond the dCypher screen to validate these interactions.

Both evaluate detailed core architecture claims (C50-C56). OpenEval finds the structural elements well-resolved and appropriate for 3.1-Å resolution. Peer reviewers also support these claims, praising the high-quality cryo-EM data and structural model.

Both evaluate comparative analysis of Arp module organization between NuA4 and SAGA (C109-C111). OpenEval finds the buried surface area calculations and interface comparisons well-supported. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these structural comparisons without raising concerns.

Both address crosslinking validation (C44, C29, C43). OpenEval finds the mapping of published CX-MS data onto the structure strongly supportive. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY and explicitly request new XL-MS experiments on the authors' own complex for independent validation, rather than relying solely on published data.

Both evaluate AlphaFold2 modeling of TINTIN module (C63-C65, C67). OpenEval supports the predictions with cautious interpretation, noting CX-MS validation. Peer reviewers accept the computational modeling integrated with experimental data without raising concerns.

Both evaluate Eaf1 scaffolding role claims (C5-C6, C48). OpenEval finds structural data and buried surface area calculations supportive, with genetic validation. Peer reviewers do not question these claims and praise the high-quality structural analysis.

Both evaluate the mechanistic recruitment model (C115-C117, C11-C12). OpenEval supports the model as logical but notes it requires in vivo validation. Peer reviewers also support the model, describing the structure as 'an important puzzle piece towards a molecular understanding of chromatin modification.'

Both evaluate structural resolution and validation claims (C2, C37-C38). OpenEval finds 3.1-Å resolution well-supported with appropriate validation methods. Peer reviewers explicitly praise 'very high quality' cryo-EM data, supporting these claims. Peer result also includes C4, C30 about flexible modules.

Both address flexible architecture claims. OpenEval evaluates C4, C30, C38-C39, C41-C42 regarding rigid hub and flexible modules as well-supported. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C3, C36, C39, C41-C42, C59, acknowledging the model is 'in much better agreement with biochemical data' without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on subunit identification (C35). OpenEval evaluates C35 as part of comprehensive structural validation including mass spectrometry and mass photometry. Peer reviewers request additional characterization (AUC, intact mass spectrometry) to confirm sample homogeneity, expressing UNCERTAINTY despite mass photometry data mentioned in manuscript.

Minimal overlap on flexible linker claims (C3, C59). OpenEval evaluates linker predictions as supported by sequence analysis and cryo-EM, noting unstructured nature is predicted rather than directly observed. Peer reviewers implicitly accept flexible architecture without specific concerns about linker predictions.

OpenEval evaluates sequential HAT complex action model (C89-C92), finding it logical based on binding data and established SAGA function, but noting in vivo validation is needed. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic sequence.

OpenEval evaluates comparative Arp module organization across NuA4, SWR1, and INO80 complexes (C104, C100-C102), finding the functional distinctions well-supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this cross-complex comparison.

OpenEval evaluates extension of flexible architecture model to other HAT complexes (C75-C76, C118-C121) as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis lacks direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this broader generalization.

OpenEval evaluates speculative TIP60 organization model (C114) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is a computational prediction without experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this TIP60-specific modeling.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C1, C13-C27) as appropriately cited and supported. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these established knowledge claims, focusing instead on novel findings.
